¶1 Auzubillah Minashaitan Nirajeem

¶2 Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim

¶3 Okay well, this is our last session but we have a very interesting topic and that is Mystical Interpretation and I hope we had more time to discuss on this issue of interpretation of the Quran by mystical insights. Of course, people would take this in many different ways and sometimes interpretation of the Quran will become like just arbitrarily tahweel giving different meanings which have no relation to the verses of the Quran. By mystical interpretation, I don't mean that type of interpretation giving sort of subjective meaning to the verses of the Quran at the will of some mystic or giving a type of meaning to the verse which is not at all attached or is not related to that verse at all.

¶4 We have many mystical interpretations written actually and a very famous Tafseer-e-Sunan which of course, we can site some examples of how he interprets for example, in the verse in which Musa tells his people that you have to kill yourself because you have done something wrong by worshiping the golden calf. Then he says, for example, it means that you have to kill you all your desires of your soul which is not very much related to the history. By mystical interpretation, also, we don't mean interpretation which are actually taken from some other ideology and given to the verses of the Quran. You find these in the Ismaili interpretation of the Quran very much. And that is, say, for example, in the interpretation by Al Qadi al Numan, an Egyptian and the greatest Ismaili scholar of all history.

¶5 He has a book Asas al-Tawil, the Foundation of Symbolic Interpretation of course, mystical interpretation of the Quran and he tries to give a type of Ismaili meaning, the Ismaili ideology as seven Imams and seven pillars into all verses of the Quran. So if for example, you mentioned the story of Noah, he said it is okay, this is again, a symbol of that, seven pillars, seven Imams and all the issues which not related at all though I don't mean this type of interpretation. What I mean by mystical interpretation? I mean a type of insightful look at the verses of the Quran, to see what means you could get from a deeper look at these verses. We have parables in the Quran.

¶6 For example, we have a Surah Noor, “Allaahu noorus samaawaati wal ard” 24:35 God is Light of the heavens and the earth. And then he says the parable or the example of its light masalu noorihee. When I say, he is light, light means what? Kamishkaatin feehaa misbaah, there were a Niche and within it a Lamp. Okay, this could be given many different meanings. I mean, if we recite the verse up to the ends, it could be given many, many different meanings. Now it's a masal, it is something that would allow us to bring closer to our mind and meaning about him, then if you look into the insight, you might find lots of meanings in it.

¶7 Ghazali wrote a book, The Niche of Light called as Mishkaat al-Anwar. It’s all a mystical interpretation of this verse. This is a very nice book, it gives us lots of insight about the verse and about Ghazali because Ghazali is known as an Ashari type of theologian but if you look into this book, Ghazali is someone who believes in wahdatul wujud, who believes in all those mystical understandings of the Quran, of the creation of very different from the Ghazali that you find in other books. So, it gives you an insight about Ghazali himself and insights about the verse. We might go through if you have time. But there is an idea, which is mentioned in Allahma Tabatabai’s Al-Mizan and he says, of course, you find some verse of the Quran giving you masal, parables example, and he says, you have to take all verses of the Quran to the example.

¶8 When Allah mentions something it is actually an allegory, it wants to bring to your mind a deeper meaning and you have to find that deeper meaning which is completely concurrent conforming with the apparent meaning and not against it. All those mystical interpretation which actually would raise objections is when the deeper meaning does not conform to the apparent meaning. Now Ghazali here of course, in his book he insists, when I give a deeper meaning of a verse, you have to have in mind that the apparent meaning doesn't go away. It is there. The literal meaning holds the deeper meaning holds as well different levels of understanding actually. And this is what we have in many verses that the Quran has deeper layers and that deeper layer of meaning has another deeper layer.

¶9 I want to give one example, tonight I need to have time to go to this Niche of life by Al-Ghazali to see how he actually goes about that verse of light. Now look at this verse in Surah Yasin. “Innaa ja'alnaa feee a'naaqihim aghlaalan fahiya ilal azqaani fahum muqmahoon. Wa ja'alnaa min baini aydeehim saddanw-wa min khalfihim saddan fa aghshai naahum fahum laa yubsiroon” 36:8,9 surely we have placed chains on their neck and these reach up to their chins so they have their heads are raised a lot. And we have made before them that barrier and a barrier behind them then we have covered them over so that they do not see. What is this? This is talking about kuffar who does not believe okay.

¶10 Now of course you go into the spirit you don't see any chain on the kuffar and their chins are not wearing like this so that they cannot because it is a type of wooden thing that they used to put on the neck and then the neck, the chin raises up. They couldn't see what's in front of them. Allah gives the parable you see. This is not a parable, Allah doesn’t say it’s a masal but it is a masal, isn't it? It is a parable. It says actually their example is not as if we have put one of those, what do you call it? Yolks on their neck. So their heads are up and the yolk is just beneath their chin.

¶11 So they cannot see what's in front of them. They walk like this and so they don't know where they are going. Not only that, not only that about kuffar, those who do not believe. Not only they will walk like this all the time, but still there is a barrier before and behind them. They cannot see anywhere and then again just behind that barrier we have covered them like they are inside the tents. They do see now they're not like this, isn't it? The kuffar would not walk like this. So this has a deeper meaning. You don't take this literally. No one would take literally. I mean, even those very stringent mufaseroon who say we have to understand or are very literally when Allah says “Ar-Rahmaanu 'alal 'Arshis tawaa” 20:5 Allah sits on the throne and there is a throne and he's sitting on it because it is what the Quran says.

¶12 So, there is a deeper meaning that means that we have covered the light, which is actually the shining light of Allah. And they are walking with their heads raised up. They don't see in front of them, what's going around them, they don't see what's going on behind them, what's come before them, and so on and so forth. Now suppose you have a verse like this, about kuffar in jahannam, what do you think about it? Can you say that, well kuffar will go in Jahannam and their heads are always raised? Well, I mean, this is the first thing that comes to mind, isn't it? And if Allah says such a thing in the Quran, you say suddenly, it's the case, they have a yoke on their neck.

¶13 And when they want to walk, they can't because there's a barrier in front of them that is behind them. They are covered in jahannam. But why this meaning and why can’t we go for another meaning? Because the thing about jahannam is that you cannot see it now. But such a thing is said about people in this world. Well, there's no suspicion there's no doubt that a deeper meaning is transparent and not the literal meaning. Now let's look at these verses about jahannam. “Halaka 'annee sultaaniyah” 69:29 my power has perished from me. This is a person who is actually taken to jahannam. “Khuzoohu faghullooh. Summal Jaheema sallooh. Summa fee silsilatin zar'uhaa sab'oona ziraa'an faslukooh” 69:30,31,32 they hold on him, then put a chain on him then cast him into the burning fire march in a chain the length of which is seven cubits.

¶14 Do you think they could put chain on him? Now, there is no doubt, isn’t it? Because we had the other verse it says that there is a yoke, chain on the kuffar in this world. Now we see people of jahannam they have chain. Is it real material type of chain or something else or a type of yolk which they put on their? Putting in a yoke, is just a real yoke or a yoke as this is mentioned in Surah Yasin about kuffar in this world. Certainly there is no doubt because I mean we can go into the deeper explanation of that verse we can go into deeper explanation of this verse as well. What is this chain the length of which is 70 cubits?

¶15 Could it be the chain of the ambitions, the chain of ignorance and the chain of everlasting long arrogant type of ambitions that they have in this world? Now they are wrapped into or this chain it might be both, but the literal meaning says that it might be both. But of course we cannot deny that it might be the real material type of chain which is put on people who are in jahannam. But we cannot deny the deeper meanings as well as they are wrapped in their lengthy ambitions that they have so that they cannot see God. Why they are put in that type of situation because they did not believe in the great Allah. Now I want to, of course, this was just to somehow see the similarity between two types of verses, one verse which speaks about kuffar in this world and one verse which is speaking about kuffar in jahannam.

¶16 And you will see that if you cannot see the chain and the yolk in this world on kuffaar, you might not be able to see in jahannam as well. It might not be in that chain and that yolk, but there is something else. And now we have another verse, “Wa man kaana fee haaziheee a'maa fahuwa fil aakhirati a'maa” 17:72 for whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the life to come as well. And we know what type of blindness Quran is talking about in this world. It wouldn't be the same blindness in the other world. They can see of course and that's what kuffar can see each other, when they go to jahannam “kullamaa dakhalat ummatul la'anat ukhtahaa” 7:38 whenever a group of people will enter they curse the previous one.

¶17 You did this to us, they know each other and they curse each other. We have many verses in the Quran that mustaqberin and mustadafin when they see each other, they talks, argue, have disputes they are not blind. So, there is a type of blindness which is similar to the blindness in this world. Now, let's go to a very interesting mystical interpretation of hell and paradise. This is very interesting. It doesn’t deny the material aspect of it but it gives you a deeper insight into what happens in hell and paradise and why people go to hell and paradise. What is the reason? This is taken from a very important book of Haji Nasiruddin Tusi, Reminder of the beginning and the end.

¶18 And interestingly enough, it is a very important mystical and philosophical book that Sadruddin Shirazi in his book “asfar al-‘aqliyya al-arba‘a” has actually translated long excerpts from this book and had put it in his book because it's a very important book. And Nasiruddin Tusi, if you remember was the one who actually wrote a commentary on Al-Isharat wa al-Tanbihat of Ibne Sina’s book that we just covered a little bit of it here. Now he says that what is maad? Maad is going back to the initial creation, but initial creation is this world. How we come to this world? In the same way we go back, it's a reverse type of process. We come into creation, this is the initial creation then we go back upwards.

¶19 Come on by the 1000 isn't having the Quran “kamaa bada akum ta'oodoon” 7:29 in the same way as he started to create you. From the same route, you go back to your lord. However in this coming and going the whole purpose of mankind being made aware either for Paradise or they go to hell of course no one is made or hell. They will go to hell due to this process of coming and going. But everyone is made for death but they can't go there before coming into this process. The way we have made the creation as we have in Surah Waqia “Wa laqad 'alimtumun nash atal oolaa falaw laa tazakkaroon” 56:62 And you certainly know already the first form of creation.

¶20 Why then do you not celebrate His praises? Why you don't take the same way back. This is the world created by God and any other world is easy for him to make like hereafter, barzakh or whatever. Now he says how we are creating this world? Let's see now, he wants to say why some people go to hell some people go to Paradise and this is a very interesting mystical interpretation of verses about Hell and Paradise. Now in this life, what you are given first is existence. “Summa min nutfatin summa min 'alaqatin summa yukhrijukum tiflan summa litablughooo” 40:67 It is He who creates you out of dust and then out of a drop of sperm and then out of a germ-cell and then He brings you forth as children.

¶21 You are given knowledge and awareness. Even when you are a baby when come to this world as a baby gradually, we have spies of the outside world, isn’t it? Our eyes spies about the things that we see, our ears spies about things that we hear, our tongues spies about the taste, what should be eaten, what shouldn't be eaten, okay. We have a very nice expression of mistakes, they say that your senses are spies of your soul; your soul cannot know what's going on except through these senses. Okay? So you are given the knowledge and awareness “Wallaahu akhrajakum mim butooni ummahaatikum laa ta'lamoona shai'an wa ja'ala lakumus sam'a wal absaara wal af'idata la'allakum tashkuroon” 16:78 when God brought you out to this world from your mother's wounds, you didn't know anything whatsoever and He gave you hearing and sight and intelligence and affections that you may give thanks (to Allah).

¶22 All these are working for him. So, then we are given knowledge and awareness, then of course, power. Initially you have no power whatsoever; gradually you can walk towards what you want. So, this is power you are given, you can shout or crawl for what you want you are given power and when you become stronger and stronger grow up, your power will increase. This is the way you are created and when of course, the most important parts of human beings will want something first of all we have to know that we are given power to obtain it and when we will something and then go and get. Now, he says to go to God, you have to somehow move back on this track.

¶23 First of all, you have to put aside your will. Now, of course not at the beginning for several years you grow like this. You have existence, knowledge of power, you have will, you move towards that but gradually God wants you to go to the opposite direction. He has clearly said this and you have to have power, will go towards what you want, take it, get it, you want to eat something and you want to have pleasure. But gradually if you want to go back, okay, you have to first of all you have to put aside your will, when you go back to God's you have to do away with first of all, your will. And this is the degree of rizaa or contentment.

¶24 When you do away with your wills, then you are content with whatever comes by God or from God. “Lahum maa yashaaa'oona feehaa wa ladainaa mazeed “50:35 if you give away your own will then your will is Will of God and so whatever you want you have it because that's the will of God. And God is of course, the way that whatever he wants he has it and if your will is a physical will that whatever you want you have it and this rizwanu mennallahi akbar which is in paradise of course, that rizwan, that contentment which you have from Allah, that's the greatest pleasure. He says something very interesting. He says, of course, we'll come through this later on as well.

¶25 But he says, the angel in charge of paradise which is called rizwan, it means you cannot enter without being content with the will of God that you have to achieve on your own and achieve the will of God to enter it. And that's how the pleasure is. This is very interesting. In jannah, there are lots of treasures, full of treasures. And the key to it is this contentment. You do away with your will go and do whatever you want. Now, you might say if you don't have any will, what do you mean by do whatever you want? No, you are given a grace and a will. A will which is everlasting, which is connected to the will of God and that's why you can go there and use that pleasures and that's why rizwan will allow you to enter.

¶26 Now what's the name of the angel which is in charge of hell? Malik. We have in the Quran, “yaa Maaliku liyaqdi 'alainaa Rabbuka” 43:77 Malik! Would that the Lord put an end to us? Because people in hell are all slaves of that angel. They are bound, they don't have any will. They can't have any will. Well he explains why they can't have any will. Here, people are given utter free will. Why? Because the will which is against the will of God is prohibited. Why? The will is in direction of the will of God and therefore whatever they want. If you remember, we talked about this hadith that at some points in jannah, an angel will bring a letter to the people of paradise from Allah.

¶27 It states that this letter is from the living who never dies to the ever-living, sustainer who never dies. The same paramount or on the same position and then he says that I am the lord and when I want something, I say be and it becomes. And from today, when you want something you say and it will become because we are the same thing. Now, he says if you do what we tell you do, we'll come to razaa then of course, you have whatever you want in paradise. Next, you have to do away with your power. You remember power was before the lord. What do you mean? Do away with your power, to know that don’t have power.

¶28 It is the power of God that you are using. And this is tawaqqul. Tawaqqul doesn't mean that you just sit down and wait for God to do. No, whatever you do you know that this is not you. This is him, this is his mercy, this power that you are using. And of course, see the meaning of the verse “wa many yatawakkal 'alal laahi fahuwa hasbuh” 65:3 and if any one puts his trust in Allah, sufficient is (Allah) for him. Whoever relies on God, knowing that the power is with him and then you have to do away with the knowledge. What do you mean by do away with the knowledge? It means that you submit to dissolve, that you don't know anything.

¶29 Only he is knowledgeable and it is He Who gives you the knowledge. Now to understand these, of course it is very complicated, very deep to understand. I advise you to read this book. This is very, very enlightening in giving meaning to these verses about tawaqqul, about submission to God. And of course he brings the verse “wa yusal limoo tasleemaa” 4:65 you have to submit completely. You remember the hades we mentioned from Ameerul Momineen, he says that knowledge has 3 spans. The first span, when you learn it you become arrogant. The second span when you learn you become humble. The third span is the span when you learn it; you know that you don’t know. You know that you have no knowledge.

¶30 We are all dependent on him if you submit completely. This is of course, the type of submission of Ibrahim “Iz qaala lahoo Rabbuhooo aslim qaala aslamtu li Rabbil 'aalameen” 2:131 when his lord said submit, I submit. Now this is a type of submission like that. Then of course you remember we said about fanaa. You have to do away with your existence and when you come to unity, you remember that existence only belongs to God. Now, of course, these things that wahdatul wujud and other things which are very complicated, okay, but you should know that your existence is a light of existence. You'd not exist. So if you come to this position, this is of course, the position of “Ulaaa'ikal lazeena an'amal laahu 'alaihim minan Nabiyyeena” 19:58.

¶31 This is a very luminous position. When you have this world, power, knowledge and existence done away, then Allah gives you new power, new existence and new knowledge. And in this way, in paradise, what you will find is, you will find ultimate consensus. That is the rizaa that you have, you will find unrestricted power because whatever power we have is restricted and limited. But if you are now drowned on the power of God, you're tacking on top power of God, not restricted at all; you can do whatever you want because now you are completely joined with that power. And you have now innate knowledge because God will give you that knowledge and that knowledge will shine in you.

¶32 Now you don't have any knowledge from yourself, that knowledge will shine in you and Paradise it is as though you know everything and also everlasting existence. You did away with your own limited existence, “zaalika yawmul khulood” 50:34. Now, let's go to the verses about hell. Now, this is what I wanted to actually to bring up here.

¶33 Q1. Not Audible

¶34 Ans: No, we reached that anyhow later on, inshallah. But this is a very good point, that not everyone can do this, isn't it? But eventually all of us will go to Paradise inshallah. We have to have this. And that's why shafaa is there to take care of us. Gradually, when we think deeper about all this, you will come to understanding that without the shafaa, it is impossible to enter paradise. It is impossible because this is not our level. This is a level which needs someone quite huge to take us there.

¶35 Q2. Not Audible

¶36 Ans: Yes, that blindness is the blindness of kufr. If you have that light of imaan, that would help and that will take you and that light of imaan is very important which is mentioned in the Quran.

¶37 Again I come to the finish of life. “Yawma taral mu'mineena walmu'minaati yas'aa nooruhum baina aydeehim: 57:12 you see that on the day the mumineen and muminaat have a light which would go ahead of them and on the right hand side. “Yaqooloona rabbanaaa atmim lanaa nooranaa” 66:8 they know that that type of light cannot take you to paradise. It is impossible. They have a light but that light is not complete. They need completion. “Yaqooloona rabbanaaa atmim lanaa nooranaa” give us so that we could come and of course, in the previous verse Allah said “yawma laa yukhzil laahun nabiyya wallazeena aamanoo” 66:8 on a Day on which God will not humiliate the Prophet and those who have belief in him.

¶38 And what is the meaning of humiliating the prophet? It means those who have said Mohammed and those who have followed him, they go to hell. It is humiliation for the Prophet, isn't it? He has done nothing wrong. He's perfect. But those who believe in him and if they go to hell, that is humiliation for him. “Yawma laa yukhzil laahun nabiyya wallazeena aamanoo ma'ahoo nooruhum yas'aa baina aydeehim wa bi aymaanihim” their Light will run forward before them So, yes, the prophet would take would complete. But if there is no light whatsoever, “Yawma yaqoolul munaafiqoona walmunaafiqaatu lil lazeena aamanu unzuroonaa naqtabis min noorikum” 57:13 One Day will the Hypocrites men and women - say to the Believers: "Wait for us!

¶39 Let us borrow (a Light) from your Light." Munafiqoon they have no light whatsoever, but those who have some light, it will be completed because Allah is not going to humiliate the prophet and prophet is going to do shafaa for these people. Now let's look at what happens in hell. Now, should a person move not in that way? What happena? Okay, he said you have to move in that way. This was coming to completion either in this world or in the next world. You go through it anyhow, either voluntarily or involuntarily, a momin should go through this process to get into paradise. However, if you don't go through it voluntarily in this world, then you have difficulty in barzakh, on the resurrection day.

¶40 You have lots of fears, lots of difficulty that you've come across. Okay, but if you have completed here, then you are from those mentioned in Surah Ambiya “Innal lazeena sabaqat lahum minnal husnaaa ulaaa'ika 'anhaa mub'adoon” 21:101 those for whom we have written good before coming to the next world, then of course they are completely far away from fear, quarrels, judgments, sirat. No, we are not tacking to those issues. They are completely away from it. “Laa yasma'oona hasee sahaa wa hum fee mash tahat anfusuhum khaalidoon” 57:102 when people are frightened from that, “Laa yahzunuhumul faza'ul akbaru wa tatalaq qaahumul malaaa'ikatu haazaa Yawmukumul lazee kuntum too'adoo” 57:103 the great fear of the Day of Judgment would not affect them if they have completed it here.

¶41 If they haven’t completed here and they haven't loved, they go to the next world of course, they have to go through that process so that they lose their will, they see that there is no power but power of God, they see there is no life but life of God. They go as per the roll book and then they enter Paradise, there are things that come out of their hearts before we enter paradise. “Wa naza'naa ma fee sudoorihim min ghillin ikhwaanan 'alaa sururim mutaqaabileen” 15:47 the mominoon when they will go to paradise that sort of grudge or envy or jealousy in the hearts about other, this should come out otherwise you cannot go to paradise. And Allah will eventually bring this out.

¶42 Should a person who's not in that direction, what happens? First of all, their wills are opposed. Well, they have a will and Allah has a will. Now whose will is going to win? Of course Allah’s, isn’t it? Now they go there with their own will and Allah’s will is not going to follow them. Why? “Wa lawit taba'al haqqu ahwaaa'ahum lafasadatis samaawaatu wal ardu” 23:71 if god wants you to follow their wills, the whole universe, the whole sky, heavens and earth would have been destroyed because I mean, the wills of people are vicious, especially the wills of kuffar are vicious. So certainly they are not. They go without will. They cannot put it aside. They cannot move without God overruling their will.

¶43 So what happens? They are always in torment. Why? As god mentions in the Quran, God cannot follow their wills. What happens, they are far from their wills. They wish something and if you want something then you come to it. This is the situation of people in the hell. If they want something it is as if they are chained, they cannot do anything. Now there are chains, the length of which is 70 cubits, of course, because of the length of the will that they have and they are chained like that. And they will deserve the wrath of God because they all the time will against the will of God and therefore they deserve the wrath of God.

¶44 So you see, is the kind of contrast between people of hell and people of paradise. “Afamanit taba'a Ridwaanal laahi kamam baaa'a bisakhatim minal laahi wa ma'waahu Jahannam” 3:162 Rizwan is for paradise, he is the one who follows the pleasure of God, he is the same as the one who returns to wrath of God because his will always oppose the will of God. And certainly, the will of god is going to overrule them. So this is one torment is hell. Now, he therefore chained, he's a slave of the Malik of hell. That Malik actually holds their wills, isn't it? Because of course, if their wills are going to be in real life, then everything would go into pieces.

¶45 So Malik holds the other slaves as Suleiman hold a jin as a slave. He didn't let them to disobey and to go over the limits. He would chain and keep them there. He doesn't let them to follow their wills because those wills will destroy the creation. Also in the hell, what happens? They are helpless, they don't have any power. Since they have lost their own power and they do not have power, they are going to use power of God. How could you use power of God? Now when you go into reality, you see that there is no power there. Here also we are using the power of God but we do not realize. If we realize it when we go to the other world, it's very easy for us.

¶46 We know how to use power of God. Now if we all the time see that how powerful you are and when you go to the other world you see that there's no power. You have no power and you don't know how to use power of god. And therefore what happens? They are left helpless. If God does not help you, leaves you helpless. “Iny-yakhzulkum faman zal lazee yansurukum min ba'dih” 3:160 and instead of taslim they have humiliation hawan, why? Because they thought that they have knowledge and there they see that they are dumb deab and blind. They have no knowledge whatsoever. So they are in humiliation. “Al yawma tujzawna 'azaabal hooni” 6:93 you will be chained, you will be revoked, you will be given the punishment of humiliation, you will be humiliated because you are arrogant in the other world.

¶47 So to whomever god humiliates, there's no one who could get dignity. There's no dignity from god in hell as well. And instead of unity with God, they use the will of God, they use the power of God they use the knowledge of God, instead of God, they have separation. And what happens of course, he will forced to go away from him and the angels would curse them to go away from him because they cannot use it. If they use it, because they have their own will they cannot use it. Now, whatever we can, I mean you can think about jahannam in many different ways. But let's think about it in this way. It is not a punishment which is brought to you by God.

¶48 God doesn't want to revenge. Don’t think that God wants to take revenge. Because then there's nothing in this world that God wants to take revenge from. It's all his creation, its only mercy that comes in. Now, the only thing is that you somehow put yourself in situation that you do not see; you don’t deserve to use the power of God, the will of God, the knowledge of God. And so, when you go back to him, you have come in this way, when you go back, you take all these wrongs with you. And then of course, you are separated from God and that separation will bring all those problems. Now, you say that, you might say that, what about the power of hell?

¶49 Those punishments, eating thorns and plants, drinking hot water; of course it’s all true. In what sense? Can anyone tell me? If this is the interpretation of hell given by greatest scholar, like Qazi Nasiruddin, what does it mean? Why shouldn't they have, although they are completely separate from God, they cannot use their own wills and the will of God and they do not know what it is. And they cannot use knowledge of God and they have no knowledge themselves. But why their physical life should be so terrible?

¶50 Ans: It's not that it becomes terrible, that they don't have the capacity to be refreshed by the capacity to be nourished by it. And therefore it's a given us the benefit in a state of suffering is the equivalent as if they were in this world drinking boiling water in this world or something like that. It is as if they are drinking boiling water.

¶51 Well, it's very difficult to go away with the literal meaning as well. But there's another interpretation that you see. There's a hades from Imam Sadiq (as) which is a very important hades. You will find the meaning everywhere. Allah created the mulk, aalamul shahadah as an example of his malaqut. So in barzakh malaqut, you have images you have things, which when they materialize in a material way in this world, they find different qualities. And of course, he created his malakut al misale jabarut. Now, you have a meaning of jabarut that would materialize in a different way in malakut and it materialized in a different way in aalamul mulk and aalamul shahadah. Now, former here for example, the burning of fire.

¶52 It is burning of fire, but if you look at it in aalmaul malakut, it is something else. The Quran is the example of those who devour the property of the orphans, they are eating fire. Now, when you look at it in malakut it is like that and when you look in jabarut it is something else. They're all much related closely. So, when you ask for the wrath of God, in the malakut people of hell it is as it is mentioned here, but in the mulk of it is fire. It materializes like that quite related to each other. So they are there. There is a very nice example given by Ghazali in the Niche of life.

¶53 He says that the prophet saw Abdul Rahman ibne Awf in his dreams that he was travelling towards paradise crown. And he says, what was the meaning of this dream that the prophet saw? Abdul Rahman is a companion of the prophet who was very rich. This he says that, yes, of course rich people cannot easily go in paradise. This is what the prophet actually concept that he saw in his dreams. So yes, there are lots of hisab there. So Abdul Rahman could not easily go to paradise. Now, if that comes to aalamul shahadah, it means that you can see as the paradise is on a hill and someone is crawling to go there. He is slow.

¶54 He said he saw the right thing. But that's why I think in malakut, it has another meaning another realization and jabarut it has another realization. And that's why you have parallel meanings. And that's why in dreams you see something while in reality it is something else. Both of them are right. Both of them are rare, but they depict that they belong to different worlds. And of course, you have all these malakut and jabarut put together here. They're in paradise in hell and so everything is somehow appropriate to this other worldly example and being under realisation. Now, let's finish, therefore, as opposed to the people of jannah, the people would have instead of ultimate contentment, they have uttered dissatisfaction.

¶55 Instead of ultimate, unlimited power, they have unlimited helplessness who cannot do anything. Instead of inborn knowledge, they have utter ignorance. Quran says that's not like existence. “Summa laa yamootu feehaa wa laa yahyaa” 87:13 they do not die, of course, but you can't call it life and can’t call it death. It's something in between. This is what I mean by insightfulness, understanding of the verses of the Quran. Let us just sticking to the very literal meaning of course, this meaning is there but there are different levels which are called mystical interpretation.

¶56 Wa sallahu ala mohammadin wa aale hittahereen
